chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Qazi narrated to us, saying: Hamid ibn Shu'ayb al-Balkhi narrated to us, saying: Bashir ibn al-Walid al-Kindi narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Yahya ibn Talha ibn Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Khalid, from Jabir ibn Samurah, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), saying:
This religion will remain sound; no one who opposes it or opposes it will harm it, until there are twelve Leaders, all of them from Quraysh.
ai.seo_question: What are the twelve leaders mentioned in the hadith of the Twelve Caliphs?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal establishes the doctrine of the Twelve Imams, emphasizing that the integrity of the faith is preserved through this specific lineage of Qurayshi leaders. It serves as a foundational text for Shia eschatology, linking the continuity of divine guidance to the political and spiritual authority of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 12-29 Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Qazi narrated that Hamid ibn Shoayb al-Balkhi quoted Bashir ibn al-Walid al-Kindi, on the authority of Ishaq ibn Yahya ibn Talha ibn Ubaydullah, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Khalid, on the authority of Jabir ibn Samurah, on the authority of God’s Prophet (MGB), “This
good religion will proceed on and no one can harm it until there come twelve Leaders after me. They are all from the Quraysh.’”
